newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian coffee bean exports rise in May.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian coffee bean exports rise in May.

text.p: Ivory Coast exported 27,788 tonnes of robusta coffee beans in May 1996/97 (October-September) against 23,324 tonnes in April and 16,300 in May 1996, official shipping data show.
Ivorian coffee exports got off to a late start in 1996/97 following low world prices in late 1996, tighter bank lending policies to exporters and quality problems slowing grading, exporters said.
May coffee exports are the highest on a monthly basis since the opening of the 1996/97 season, which has yielded Ivory Coast's largest crop since the early 1980s.
The data showed 23,964 tonnes of May exports went from Abidjan, the main port, with 3,824 tonnes shipped from Ivory Coast's second port, San Pedro.
Cumulative bean exports in the first eight months of the 1996/97 season were 89,878 tonnes against 98,108 tonnes in the same period of 1995/96 and 74,517 in 1994/95.
Coffee product exports, from Abidjan, included 803 tonnes of soluble coffee.
Ivorian coffee arrivals totalled around 307,000 tonnes by July 11, leaving large stocks remaining to be shipped.
Ivory Coast has forecast a 1996/97 crop of 230,000 tonnes, against 180,000 tonnes recorded last year.
Exporters said they would raise coffee sorting and grading capacity in 1997/98 to avoid the problems met this year.
